card.description: A period-three dynamical stabilizer memory made only from weight-two Pauli measurements on a honeycomb torus. Edge operators are fixed as XX, YY, or ZZ by direction, while a plaquette three-coloring partitions them into three perfect-matching rounds. The code is the ordered schedule and its outcome-dependent instantaneous stabilizer group, not any one static set of mutually commuting edge checks; after startup that group carries two toric-code logical qubits.

views.description: After the declared startup, the constructor exports independent sign-free Pauli generators for one instantaneous stabilizer group as a symplectic CheckMatrix. This is the universal R1 snapshot for rank and commutation; it does not determine the protocol's spacetime distance.

The executable object is a three-round Schedule. An incoming matching replaces anticommuting generators in the instantaneous stabilizer group while preserving a rank-eight plaquette backbone; this view distinguishes the dynamical code from a frozen check matrix.

Contract every edge measured in the latest round into an effective qubit. The resulting instantaneous stabilizer group is locally Clifford-equivalent to a toric code, which explains the two logical qubits without identifying the full spacetime protocol with a static toric memory.

Plaquette information is assembled from measurement outcomes at different times. Faults are classified by the detector events they create and by whether an undetectable spacetime history is benign, so circuit fault distance cannot be read from one instantaneous snapshot.

Kitaev's four-Majorana representation factors each directional Pauli edge into a Z2 gauge variable and a matter-fermion pairing. The measurement cycle then becomes a rotating pairing pattern whose gauge-invariant products are the plaquette fluxes.

One full code period transports the instantaneous toric order through a protected cycle and exchanges electric and magnetic anyon labels. This separates preservation of a logical subspace from the nontrivial logical frame motion performed by the memory schedule itself.

A ZX diagram represents the whole measurement history as a spacetime tensor network. Different circuit, fusion, and Floquet descriptions can be related by local rewrites without pretending that their hardware noise models are identical.

intuition:
# Honeycomb Floquet code

## Essence

**The object.** Put one qubit on every vertex of a honeycomb torus. Every edge
has a direction label `x`, `y`, or `z` and carries the corresponding two-qubit
measurement `XX`, `YY`, or `ZZ`. A proper three-coloring of the hexagons gives
a second, independent edge label: the color missing from the two faces beside
that edge. At round `r`, measure all edges with missing color `r`. Those edges
form a perfect matching, so the measurements within one round commute even
though adjacent edge operators from different rounds anticommute.

That ordered, period-three measurement schedule is the code. The edge
operators are not a static stabilizer group. Instead, past outcomes define an
instantaneous stabilizer group (ISG) that is updated whenever the next
matching is measured. On the shipped `3 x 3` torus, the constructor tracks the
startup ranks

`9, 12, 14, 16, 16, 16, ...`

after successive rounds. The steady rank is `16` on `18` qubits, so two
logical qubits survive indefinitely. The reproduction script recomputes this
profile, the two-logical-qubit `6 x 6` instance, every perfect matching, and
the plaquette backbone; see the
[schedule and ISG derivation](pedagogy/schedule-isg-cycle.md). The executable
transcript is shipped as `pedagogy/reproduce.py`.

**The invariant.** Multiply the six directional edge operators around one
hexagon. At each vertex two different Pauli letters meet, leaving the third;
the product is a weight-six plaquette Pauli. It commutes with every edge
measurement and therefore survives all three rounds. On the `3 x 3` torus the
nine plaquette products have rank eight. Combining them with any steady-round
matching gives rank sixteen, with one shared dependency. This permanent
backbone plus one moving matching is the algebraic skeleton of the ISG.

**The post-struggle sentence.** Honeycomb protection comes from measuring
three incompatible perfect matchings in the right order: invariant plaquette
products remember the syndrome, while the currently measured matching
continually redraws a toric-code frame around two logical qubits.

## Design problem

Weight-two parity measurements are attractive because several hardware
architectures can implement them more directly than high-weight stabilizer
measurements. The obstruction is immediate. Two honeycomb edges meeting at a
vertex carry different Pauli letters, so their two-qubit operators
anticommute. No static stabilizer code can contain every edge operator.

The static-subsystem shortcut also fails. If all edge operators are declared
gauge generators, their center contains the plaquette products but the parent
subsystem group does not carry the two logical qubits generated by the
Floquet protocol. The information lives in the order of measurements and in
the outcome-dependent update rule, not in the common center alone. This is
the foundational distinction made by
[Hastings and Haah](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.02194).

The schedule solves three constraints simultaneously:

1. every round must be a perfect matching, so its measurements commute and
   touch every qubit exactly once;
2. the incoming matching must replace, rather than accumulate with, the
   anticommuting part of the previous ISG;
3. products of outcomes across time must expose stable plaquette information
   for a decoder.

The plaquette three-coloring supplies the needed matchings. Crucially, the
round label is not the edge-direction label. Each shipped round contains
equal numbers of `XX`, `YY`, and `ZZ` measurements. Grouping by direction
instead produces a valid-looking three-round schedule with the wrong
steady-state logical count. The
[wrong-schedule counterexample](pedagogy/schedule-isg-cycle.md#the-direction-grouped-counterexample)
is therefore part of the definition, not a coding-style warning.

The bargain is sharp: the code gains topological memory from weight-two
measurements, but syndrome information is spread over time. A decoder must
know the schedule, measurement circuit, detector definitions, and noise
normalization. A static parity-check matrix is insufficient.

## Derivation chain

**1. Separate direction from round.** For `L1 x L2` unit cells there are two
vertices per cell and hence `n = 2 L1 L2` qubits. The three geometric
directions determine Pauli type. A three-coloring of faces determines round.
For every edge, the two adjacent face colors are distinct; the unused color
is its round label.

**2. Prove that a round is measurable.** At a trivalent vertex, the three
incident edges separate the three pairs of neighboring face colors, so their
missing colors are all different. Exactly one edge of each round label meets
the vertex. Each round is therefore a disjoint union of edges covering every
qubit once: a perfect matching. The constructor checks this exact support
condition before returning a `Schedule`.

**3. Build the invariant plaquettes.** Let `W_p` be the product of the six
directional edge operators around face `p`. A boundary edge overlaps `W_p` at
two endpoints and contributes two local anticommutations. A non-boundary edge
touching the face meets it at one vertex, but `W_p` carries the same Pauli
letter there as that outward edge. Both cases commute. Thus every `W_p`
commutes with every measurement in every round. The
[plaquette calculation](pedagogy/schedule-isg-cycle.md#the-rank-eight-plaquette-backbone)
gives the explicit `3 x 3` words and the single global dependency.

**4. Update the ISG rather than append checks.** Suppose an incoming measured
Pauli anticommutes with old ISG generators. Choose one such generator as a
pivot, multiply it into the other anticommuting generators so they commute
with the measurement, and replace the pivot by the measured Pauli. This
preserves mutual commutation and is exactly the sign-free rule implemented by
`ISGTracker.measure`. After startup, each round replaces the moving matching
while the plaquette subgroup remains.

**5. Count what survives the whole sequence.** The static snapshot returned
by `constructor.py` has rank sixteen and therefore `k = 18 - 16 = 2`.
Independently, the schedule verifier evolves full periods until the rank
profile repeats and computes `dynamic_k = n - periodic_rank = 2`. Equality of
the two counts is a consistency check. A wrong schedule can have a plausible
snapshot at one time and a different long-time count, so the Atlas records
both properties.

**6. Contract the latest matching.** Fuse the two physical qubits on each
just-measured edge into one effective qubit. Under a depth-one local Clifford
change of basis, the moving checks and plaquette products become star and
plaquette stabilizers of a coarser toric lattice. This explains two torus
logical qubits at each steady time. The map changes from round to round,
which is why the full protocol carries a nontrivial anyon automorphism rather
than being one frozen toric code. The full dictionary lives on the
[instantaneous toric-frame page](pedagogy/toric-frame-automorphism.md).

**7. Turn outcomes into detectors.** An individual edge outcome is random
gauge information. A plaquette value is inferred from a prescribed product
of outcomes gathered at different times; comparing successive inferred
values produces a detection event. Physical faults become edges or
hyperedges in a spacetime detector model. The
[detector and distance page](pedagogy/spacetime-detectors-distance.md)
separates this circuit fault distance from any static snapshot distance.

## Multiple pictures

- **Schedule / ISG.** This is the executable Atlas representation. It answers
  which operators are measured, in what order, and how many logical qubits
  survive the repeated update. The landing-page explorer reads the exported
  schedule directly. Its constructor-derived coordinates form an equal-edge
  honeycomb in one periodic fundamental domain. Matching teal or violet arrows
  identify opposite sides, so a measurement cut by the displayed boundary is
  still one local edge on the torus rather than a long edge across the patch.

- **Invariant plaquettes plus a moving matching.** At a fixed steady time, the
  rank-eight plaquette subgroup is permanent and one matching supplies the
  changing local frame. This is the shortest algebraic explanation of why
  incompatible edge checks do not simply measure away the code.

- **Instantaneous toric code.** Contracting the most recent matching exposes a
  toric stabilizer group. This picture explains the two logical qubits and
  winding strings, but it does not include measurement faults or time ordering.
  See the [toric-frame dictionary](pedagogy/toric-frame-automorphism.md).

- **Spacetime detector complex.** Outcomes live on measurement events, while
  detectors relate events at different times. An error is classified by its
  detector boundary and logical action in spacetime. This is the correct
  picture for matching, timelike distance, leakage, and circuit thresholds;
  see the [decoder ledger](pedagogy/decoding-circuit-ledger.md).

- **Majorana / parton gauge theory.** Kitaev's representation writes each spin
  using four Majoranas and a local parity constraint. A directional Pauli edge
  factors into a `Z2` gauge link and a matter-Majorana pairing. Plaquette
  products become gauge fluxes; changing rounds re-pairs matter Majoranas.
  The exact correspondences and their limits are on the
  [representation dictionary](pedagogy/representation-dictionary.md).

- **Anyon automorphism and measurement QCA.** The sequence transports the
  instantaneous toric order and exchanges electric and magnetic labels after
  a period. On a boundary, the same protocol is a measurement quantum cellular
  automaton with information flow not visible in bulk rank. This picture is
  best for logical operations and boundary anomalies.

- **ZX spacetime.** A ZX network treats preparation, parity measurement,
  fusion, and Floquet schedules as alternative spacetime slicings related by
  local rewrites. It is useful for translating protocol structure, but it
  does not make two implementations share a noise model.

## Why these parameters

**Why `n = 2 L1 L2`.** The chosen periodic cell contains one `A` and one `B`
vertex. `constructor.py` enumerates exactly `L1 L2` cells and creates three
edges per cell, giving a trivalent graph with `2 L1 L2` vertices.

**Why both lengths are multiples of three.** The dual graph of honeycomb faces
is triangular. In the constructor's torus convention, the coloring
`c(i,j) = i - j mod 3` must return to itself around both periodic handles.
The two winding conditions require `L1 = 0 mod 3` and `L2 = 0 mod 3`.
The reproduction script exhausts all dimensions from two through nine and
confirms that the constraint solver finds a proper coloring exactly for those
pairs. Invalid sizes fail loudly instead of returning a different schedule.

**Why period three.** Three face colors produce three missing-color edge
classes, and every vertex meets one edge from each class. Fewer classes cannot
partition all three incident directions into perfect matchings while retaining
the same plaquette-color construction.

**Why `k = dynamic_k = 2` on the torus.** Nine plaquettes have rank eight.
At a steady time, the current matching has rank nine, and its span intersects
the plaquette span in one global relation. The ISG rank is therefore
`8 + 9 - 1 = 16`; subtracting from eighteen leaves two. The `6 x 6` instance
independently reaches rank seventy on seventy-two qubits. These are recomputed
facts, not parameter formulas copied from a paper.

**Why no `d` appears in `instances.yaml`.** The exact distance of the frozen
ISG is not the operational distance of a noisy periodic measurement protocol.
Floquet fault distance minimizes over undetectable, non-benign spacetime error
histories and depends on the circuit and observation window. The present
verifier has no such computation, so the entry leaves `d` unknown rather than
mislabeling a snapshot distance. The formal gap is explained on the
[distance page](pedagogy/spacetime-detectors-distance.md).

## Failure modes

- **Grouping by Pauli direction.** Measuring every `XX` edge, then every `YY`
  edge, then every `ZZ` edge also gives three perfect matchings and preserves
  the plaquette products. It is nevertheless a different dynamical code. The
  reproduction anti-test finds `dynamic_k = 20` on its `6 x 6` torus, while
  the plaquette-color schedule has `dynamic_k = 2`. Local commutation and a
  surviving center are not sufficient certificates.

- **Reading distance from one frame.** The instantaneous toric equivalence
  does not turn circuit faults into a static toric syndrome. Measurement
  errors, time boundaries, and benign spacetime deformations are missing from
  that snapshot. Thresholds and fault distances must name a circuit and
  detector model.

- **Transplanting thresholds.** The six-step CNOT circuit, native entangling
  measurement model, planar boundary circuits, Majorana parity model, and
  photonic loss model have different locations and correlations. Their
  thresholds are not interchangeable properties of `card.yaml`'s
  `CheckMatrix`; the [quantitative ledger](pedagogy/decoding-circuit-ledger.md)
  keeps each number attached to its experiment.

- **Confusing the Kitaev Hamiltonian with this code.** The static honeycomb
  spin model supplies the directional operators and Majorana language. Its
  ground-state phase diagram is not a realization of a repeated
  measurement-only memory.

- **Treating every honeycomb-layout code as this schedule.** CSS honeycomb,
  X3Z3, hyperbolic, qudit, twist-network, and higher-dimensional descendants
  alter independent axes: Pauli pattern, geometry, boundaries, or circuit.
  The [variant map](pedagogy/boundaries-variants.md) states which claims do
  and do not transfer.

- **Ignoring startup and readout.** The steady ISG emerges only after
  measurements establish enough outcome constraints. A real memory experiment
  also needs state preparation, detector-boundary conventions, final logical
  readout, and a decoder that handles both temporal ends.

## Operations story

The unmodified memory schedule already performs a logical-frame action. In
the instantaneous toric description, one period exchanges electric and
magnetic anyon labels. A winding representative that is electric in one frame
must therefore be redressed and interpreted as magnetic in the next. Two
periods restore the anyon label, although outcome-dependent Pauli-frame updates
still have to be tracked. This is a measurement-based topological Clifford
automorphism, not a transversal gate on a fixed block.

More elaborate operations change geometry or schedule:

- condensation lines and twist endpoints can be created, moved, fused, and
  braided while retaining two-body measurements;
- a non-orientable cross-cap geometry makes one period act as logical `HZ` on
  its encoded qubit, with folding providing a bilayer implementation;
- general automorphism-code and fixed-point-circuit frameworks explain how
  protected paths act on anyon labels.

These mechanisms and their assumptions are separated on the
[logical-operations page](pedagogy/logical-operations.md). The six-lens sweep
searched through 2026-07-26 and found no complete universal, fully benchmarked
gate set for the unmodified planar Hastings-Haah memory. Results for Floquet
color codes or Floquet-Bacon-Shor are neighboring protocols, not native
honeycomb operations.

## Litmus questions

**Q1:** Why do repeated incompatible measurements not accumulate until
`k = 0`? **A:** An incoming measurement is not blindly appended to the ISG.
When it anticommutes with old generators, the update rule replaces one pivot
and multiplies that pivot into the other anticommuting rows. The rank-eight
plaquette subgroup survives, while the moving matching is exchanged for the
new one. Direct evolution reaches rank sixteen and then repeats, leaving two
logical qubits.

**Q2:** What are the two different labels on an edge? **A:** Its geometric
direction chooses the Pauli letter `X`, `Y`, or `Z`. The missing color of its
two adjacent plaquettes chooses measurement round `0`, `1`, or `2`. Confusing
these labels produces the direction-grouped counterexample. Every correct
round in the shipped `3 x 3` schedule contains three measurements of each
Pauli type.

**Q3:** Why is `dynamic_k` needed when the snapshot already reports `k = 2`?
**A:** Snapshot `k` counts the centralizer quotient of one frozen ISG.
`dynamic_k` first evolves the repeated schedule to its periodic rank and asks
how many qubits survive the entire sequence. Their agreement certifies this
constructor; wrong schedules can make the two notions diverge or stabilize at
the wrong family scaling.

**Q4:** Can the toric-code distance be quoted as the Honeycomb fault distance?
**A:** No. The local Clifford contraction describes an instantaneous
stabilizer frame. Circuit fault distance classifies complete spacetime error
histories modulo benign errors, including faulty measurements and temporal
boundaries. Until that detector circuit is specified and analyzed, the Atlas
leaves `d` unclaimed.

**Q5:** What did the hardware evidence establish as of the 2026-07-26
literature sweep? **A:** The literal IBM experiment measured Honeycomb
plaquette stabilizers and reported syndrome-change behavior, but it did not
demonstrate a repeatedly protected logical memory or distance scaling.
Majorana, photonic, fabrication-defect, and dynamic-circuit results in the
sweep are proposals or simulations. The
[realization ledger](pedagogy/realization-ledger.md) keeps those boundaries
explicit.

independently reaches rank seventy on seventy-two qubits. These are recomputed
facts, not parameter formulas copied from a paper.

**Why no `d` appears in `instances.yaml`.** The exact distance of the frozen
ISG is not the operational distance of a noisy periodic measurement protocol.
Floquet fault distance minimizes over undetectable, non-benign spacetime error
histories and depends on the circuit and observation window. The present
verifier has no such computation, so the entry leaves `d` unknown rather than
mislabeling a snapshot distance. The formal gap is explained on the
[distance page](pedagogy/spacetime-detectors-distance.md).

## Failure modes

- **Grouping by Pauli direction.** Measuring every `XX` edge, then every `YY`
  edge, then every `ZZ` edge also gives three perfect matchings and preserves
  the plaquette products. It is nevertheless a different dynamical code. The
  reproduction anti-test finds `dynamic_k = 20` on its `6 x 6` torus, while
  the plaquette-color schedule has `dynamic_k = 2`. Local commutation and a
  surviving center are not sufficient certificates.

- **Reading distance from one frame.** The instantaneous toric equivalence
  does not turn circuit faults into a static toric syndrome. Measurement
  errors, time boundaries, and benign spacetime deformations are missing from
  that snapshot. Thresholds and fault distances must name a circuit and
  detector model.

- **Transplanting thresholds.** The six-step CNOT circuit, native entangling
  measurement model, planar boundary circuits, Majorana parity model, and
  photonic loss model have different locations and correlations. Their
  thresholds are not interchangeable properties of `card.yaml`'s
  `CheckMatrix`; the [quantitative ledger](pedagogy/decoding-circuit-ledger.md)
  keeps each number attached to its experiment.

- **Confusing the Kitaev Hamiltonian with this code.** The static honeycomb
  spin model supplies the directional operators and Majorana language. Its
  ground-state phase diagram is not a realization of a repeated
  measurement-only memory.

- **Treating every honeycomb-layout code as this schedule.** CSS honeycomb,
  X3Z3, hyperbolic, qudit, twist-network, and higher-dimensional descendants
  alter independent axes: Pauli pattern, geometry, boundaries, or circuit.
  The [variant map](pedagogy/boundaries-variants.md) states which claims do
  and do not transfer.

- **Ignoring startup and readout.** The steady ISG emerges only after
  measurements establish enough outcome constraints. A real memory experiment
  also needs state preparation, detector-boundary conventions, final logical
  readout, and a decoder that handles both temporal ends.

## Operations story

The unmodified memory schedule already performs a logical-frame action. In
the instantaneous toric description, one period exchanges electric and
magnetic anyon labels. A winding representative that is electric in one frame
must therefore be redressed and interpreted as magnetic in the next. Two
periods restore the anyon label, although outcome-dependent Pauli-frame updates
still have to be tracked. This is a measurement-based topological Clifford
automorphism, not a transversal gate on a fixed block.

More elaborate operations change geometry or schedule:

- condensation lines and twist endpoints can be created, moved, fused, and
  braided while retaining two-body measurements;
- a non-orientable cross-cap geometry makes one period act as logical `HZ` on
  its encoded qubit, with folding providing a bilayer implementation;
- general automorphism-code and fixed-point-circuit frameworks explain how
  protected paths act on anyon labels.

These mechanisms and their assumptions are separated on the
[logical-operations page](pedagogy/logical-operations.md). The six-lens sweep
searched through 2026-07-26 and found no complete universal, fully benchmarked
gate set for the unmodified planar Hastings-Haah memory. Results for Floquet
color codes or Floquet-Bacon-Shor are neighboring protocols, not native
honeycomb operations.

## Litmus questions

**Q1:** Why do repeated incompatible measurements not accumulate until
`k = 0`? **A:** An incoming measurement is not blindly appended to the ISG.
When it anticommutes with old generators, the update rule replaces one pivot
and multiplies that pivot into the other anticommuting rows. The rank-eight
plaquette subgroup survives, while the moving matching is exchanged for the
new one. Direct evolution reaches rank sixteen and then repeats, leaving two
logical qubits.

**Q2:** What are the two different labels on an edge? **A:** Its geometric
direction chooses the Pauli letter `X`, `Y`, or `Z`. The missing color of its
two adjacent plaquettes chooses measurement round `0`, `1`, or `2`. Confusing
these labels produces the direction-grouped counterexample. Every correct
round in the shipped `3 x 3` schedule contains three measurements of each
Pauli type.

**Q3:** Why is `dynamic_k` needed when the snapshot already reports `k = 2`?
**A:** Snapshot `k` counts the centralizer quotient of one frozen ISG.
`dynamic_k` first evolves the repeated schedule to its periodic rank and asks
how many qubits survive the entire sequence. Their agreement certifies this
constructor; wrong schedules can make the two notions diverge or stabilize at
the wrong family scaling.

**Q4:** Can the toric-code distance be quoted as the Honeycomb fault distance?
**A:** No. The local Clifford contraction describes an instantaneous
stabilizer frame. Circuit fault distance classifies complete spacetime error
histories modulo benign errors, including faulty measurements and temporal
boundaries. Until that detector circuit is specified and analyzed, the Atlas
leaves `d` unclaimed.

**Q5:** What did the hardware evidence establish as of the 2026-07-26
literature sweep? **A:** The literal IBM experiment measured Honeycomb
plaquette stabilizers and reported syndrome-change behavior, but it did not
demonstrate a repeatedly protected logical memory or distance scaling.
Majorana, photonic, fabrication-defect, and dynamic-circuit results in the
sweep are proposals or simulations. The
[realization ledger](pedagogy/realization-ledger.md) keeps those boundaries
explicit.

documents.title: Boundaries and variant axes
documents.markdown:
# Boundaries and variant axes

Honeycomb geometry, Pauli schedule, boundary termination, qudit dimension,
and physical circuit are independent design axes. This map prevents results
from one axis choice from being silently attached to another.

## Open boundaries

[Planar Floquet Codes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.05348) shows why a large
instantaneous distance is not enough: short spacetime fault paths can use a
boundary and the measurement order. Boundaries must be designed together
with detectors.

[Boundaries for the Honeycomb Code](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.09545) gives
terminations compatible with the original Pauli pattern and planar logical
encodings. This Atlas constructor implements only closed tori. It does not
infer a planar patch by deleting wraparound edges because doing so would omit
boundary checks, schedule changes, detector endpoints, and readout rules.

## Pauli-pattern variants

- **CSS honeycomb.**
  [Davydova, Tantivasadakarn, and Balasubramanian](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.02468)
  introduce schedules with CSS measurements and no parent subsystem code. The
  shared lattice does not make its ISG, detector graph, or gate set identical
  to the Hastings-Haah code.
- **X3Z3.**
  [Setiawan and McLauchlan](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04974) tailor a
  dynamical code to biased noise and retain a stabilizer-product symmetry. Its
  bias performance belongs to its changed Pauli pattern and circuits.
- **Aperiodic dynamic trees.** Switching among schedules changes the temporal
  code itself; period-three rank checks do not certify an aperiodic protocol.

## Geometry variants

- **Hyperbolic Floquet codes.**
  [Negative-curvature constructions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.10033) trade
  Euclidean locality for finite rate and logarithmic distance. A reported
  `[[400,52,8]]` instance and its thresholds are properties of that hyperbolic
  family, not a large honeycomb torus.
- **Twist networks.** Condensation lines and twist endpoints change the defect
  content while retaining trivalent connectivity and two-body measurements.
- **Three-dimensional descendants.** Tricoordinated 3D schedules can realize
  fermionic toric or fracton orders with different logical sectors. They are
  not additional `(L1,L2)` instances of this entry.

## Hardware and fabrication variants

[McLauchlan, Gehér, and Moylett](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15854) remove
defective qubits and stabilizers without adding connectivity, then simulate
planar performance under a fabrication-defect model. Their roughly `12%`
fabrication-defect tolerance is tied to that prescription and model. Deleting
a vertex from the torus constructor without implementing the compensating
schedule would not reproduce it.

[Claes's dynamic circuit](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.08069) changes which
physical qubits act as data and measurement resources. Majorana and
spin-photonic proposals change the native fault alphabet. These are circuit
variants even when the ideal parity graph looks familiar.

## Qudit and defect generalizations

Twist constructions extend the schedule to `Z_N` qudits and use
fermion-condensation lines for protected processing. Qudit commutation phases,
detector values, and decoder alphabets differ from binary symplectic
arithmetic. The present `Pauli` and `CheckMatrix` objects are qubit-only and
do not machine-certify those variants.

## Transfer matrix

| claim | torus original | planar original | CSS/X3Z3 | hyperbolic/qudit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| local weight-two ideal checks | yes | often | often | construction-dependent |
| shipped `dynamic_k = 2` | yes | no transfer | no transfer | no transfer |
| torus face-color constraint | yes | boundary removes it | schedule-dependent | geometry-dependent |
| periodic MWPM graph | source model | rebuild boundaries | rebuild Pauli/circuit model | rebuild geometry |
| original anyon exchange | source result | boundary action needs analysis | variant-dependent | phase-dependent |

The safe rule is simple: locality may transfer as motivation; logical counts,
distance, thresholds, and operations require a fresh certificate.

documents.title: Decoder and circuit ledger
documents.markdown:
# Decoder and circuit ledger

“Decoded by matching” is incomplete. The graph, weights, correlation
approximation, circuit, and noise normalization determine the actual decoder
experiment.

## Core periodic-memory construction

[Gidney, Newman, Fowler, and Broughton](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.10457)
derive two interleaved spacetime matching graphs for the honeycomb memory.
Detector events are vertices. Single modeled faults connect the detectors
they can trigger, and edge weights come from the circuit-level fault
probabilities. Correlation-aware minimum-weight perfect matching then chooses
a likely fault class consistent with the observed boundary.

The paper reports threshold ranges of approximately:

- `0.2%--0.3%` for its six-step CNOT-based parity circuit;
- `1.5%--2.0%` for its native entangling-measurement model.

These are literature claims under the paper's respective noise
normalizations. They are not recomputed by `constructor.py`, and the
difference between the ranges is evidence that “Honeycomb threshold” is not a
well-defined phrase without the circuit model.

## Planar benchmark models

[Benchmarking the Planar Honeycomb Code](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.11845)
separates SD6, SI1000, and EM3 circuit assumptions. They differ in native
operations, error locations, and normalization. Opening the torus also adds
spatial boundary nodes and changes which fault chains are logically
nontrivial.

Consequently, a fair comparison must hold fixed:

- the planar patch and boundary types;
- the number of syndrome rounds and temporal boundary rules;
- the circuit schedule and native operation set;
- the probability assigned to each fault location;
- decoder correlation handling;
- whether performance is quoted per logical qubit, per round, or per unit
  spacetime volume.

## Majorana-native models

[Paetznick et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.11829) construct explicit
Majorana parity-measurement circuits and their detector models. Poisoning and
correlated parity faults do not map term-for-term onto depolarizing
two-qubit-gate noise. The hardware motivation—native weight-two parity—is
therefore also a warning against importing a superconducting threshold.

## Biased noise and changed schedules

The [X3Z3 variant](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04974) changes the Pauli pattern
to preserve bias. Its detector symmetry and matching simplifications belong
to that variant, not to the unmodified Hastings-Haah schedule. Setiawan and
McLauchlan also identify an obstruction to reducing the studied two-body
dynamical class to one-dimensional decoding graphs. A favorable bias does
not automatically make the original honeycomb graph one-dimensional.

## Leakage and dynamic circuits

[A Dynamic Circuit for the Honeycomb Floquet Code](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.08069)
changes physical roles during the cycle so measured/reset qubits remove
leakage and timelike distance improves. Once the circuit changes, detector
definitions and graph weights must be regenerated. “Same ideal edge
measurements” does not imply “same fault-tolerant code.”

## Beyond pair matching

One physical fault may activate more than two detectors. A graph decoder
either decomposes such correlations into weighted edges or supplements
matching with correlation updates. Hypergraph or logical-class methods can
retain different information. The
[2026 worm-decoder work](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.05428) includes honeycomb
Floquet examples by sampling logical-class probabilities, but this is a
research decoder rather than a replacement for the registered standard MWPM
row.

## Acceptance checklist for a number

Before copying any threshold or logical-error rate, require all of:

1. exact code variant and boundary;
2. ideal measurement schedule;
3. physical parity circuit;
4. noise channel and probability normalization;
5. detector construction;
6. decoder and correlation treatment;
7. size/time scaling and fitted observable.

If any item changes, the number is a new experiment. `card.yaml` therefore
stores circuit-qualified decoder notes rather than a bare threshold field.

documents.title: Honeycomb Floquet code — Level-2 map
documents.markdown:
# Honeycomb Floquet code — Level-2 map

The schedule, instantaneous code, spacetime detector model, and physical
circuit answer different questions. This index keeps their claims separate
and links each long argument exactly once.

1. [From plaquette coloring to a periodic ISG](schedule-isg-cycle.md):
   the two edge labels, perfect-matching proof, weight-six plaquette
   invariants, startup rank profile, steady rank count, torus-coloring
   constraint, and the direction-grouped anti-test.
2. [The instantaneous toric frame and its anyon automorphism](toric-frame-automorphism.md):
   contraction of the latest matching, the effective toric stabilizers,
   winding logicals, redressing between rounds, and the electric-magnetic
   exchange after one period.
3. [Detectors and distance live in spacetime](spacetime-detectors-distance.md):
   how random edge outcomes become plaquette detectors, why snapshot distance
   is insufficient, and what a future machine verifier must compute.
4. [Decoder and circuit ledger](decoding-circuit-ledger.md):
   correlated matching, circuit/noise-model boundaries, threshold
   normalization, leakage, and the quantitative claims that must not be
   transferred between models.
5. [Boundaries and variant axes](boundaries-variants.md):
   planar termination, CSS, X3Z3, hyperbolic, twist, qudit, fabrication-defect,
   and higher-dimensional relatives, with an explicit map of non-transferable
   claims.
6. [Logical operations from automorphisms, twists, and geometry](logical-operations.md):
   the native electric-magnetic frame cycle, twist-defect processing,
   cross-cap gates, and the boundary of the known gate set.
7. [What hardware has and has not demonstrated](realization-ledger.md):
   the literal IBM plaquette experiment separated from Majorana, photonic,
   dynamic-circuit, and adjacent Floquet evidence.
8. [Representation dictionary](representation-dictionary.md):
   schedule/ISG, instantaneous toric, Majorana, detector, anyon-automorphism,
   measurement-QCA, and ZX-spacetime views, including the conversions that
   remain curated.

## Reproduction contract

Run from the repository root:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
python atlas/honeycomb/pedagogy/reproduce.py
make verify-entry E=atlas/honeycomb
```

`reproduce.py` loads the shipped entry and recomputes both reference
instances, the `3 x 3` startup rank profile, steady periodic rank,
`dynamic_k`, perfect-matching and mixed-Pauli properties, the rank-eight
plaquette backbone, representative measurement supports, all small
torus-colorability decisions from dimensions two through nine, and the
`6 x 6` direction-grouped counterexample. The ordinary verifier separately
checks every structured claim in `instances.yaml`.

The `construction:` recipe now binds `L1,L2` into
`honeycomb_torus_schedule@1`, whose pinned convention fixes vertices, faces,
plaquette colors, rounds, and measurement order. The
`plaquette_colored_floquet@1` operation applies the fixed six-period ISG
burn-in and must reproduce the ordinary constructor's complete stabilizer
array for both shipped tori. Construction replay v1 compares that final
`CheckMatrix`; the reproduction transcript separately checks the intervening
schedule and phase-by-phase ISG facts.

## Provenance split

- **Recomputed facts:** `n`, snapshot `k`, non-CSS presentation, periodic
  `dynamic_k`, the full startup rank profile, round period and perfect
  matchings, equal `XX`/`YY`/`ZZ` counts within each round, plaquette weights
  and rank, the face-coloring constraint over the documented scan, and the
  direction-grouped anti-test.
- **Bounded facts:** none. The entry intentionally makes no static or
  spacetime `d` claim, so it does not attach a seeded witness to an
  inapplicable distance definition.
- **Literature claims:** instantaneous local-Clifford equivalence to toric
  code, electric-magnetic anyon exchange, detector constructions, thresholds,
  benign-error distance theory, boundary and variant behavior, logical
  operations, and every hardware result. Each depends on an analytical map,
  circuit, decoder, geometry, or device not reproduced by the current
  constructor.
- **Citation reconciliation:** the fetch-verified sweep used
  `hastings2021dynamical` and `gidney2021honeycomb`; the controlled registry
  records them as aliases of the canonical structured keys
  `hastings2021dynamically` and `gidney2021fault`. This entry uses the
  canonical keys.

documents.title: Logical operations from automorphisms, twists, and geometry
documents.markdown:
# Logical operations from automorphisms, twists, and geometry

Floquet logical operations act by transporting an encoded space through a
sequence of code frames. They are not ordinary transversal gates on one
fixed stabilizer block.

## Native electric-magnetic exchange

After each round, contracting the measured matching exposes an instantaneous
toric frame. Composing the three frame changes around one period exchanges
the toric anyons `e` and `m`. A logical winding string of electric character
is transported to magnetic character, and vice versa.

The operation is protected because it is induced by a local path through
topologically ordered frames. Its physical cost is continued execution of the
memory schedule plus classical tracking of measurement outcomes and logical
representatives. Two periods restore the anyon label. This is the first
operation recorded in `card.yaml`.

## Twist-defect processing

[Floquet Codes with a Twist](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.08027) introduces
fermion-condensation lines whose endpoints are twists. Schedule deformations
can create, move, fuse, and braid these endpoints while keeping two-body
measurements and trivalent connectivity.

The logical action belongs to the topology of defect worldlines, but fault
tolerance still requires repeated syndrome extraction around the moving
defects. A static picture of twist locations does not specify hook errors,
time separation, or decoder boundaries.

[Floquet Codes and Phases in Twist-Defect Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17664)
places these operations in a broader classification of phases and anyon
permutations. The classification tells which automorphism is possible; it
does not by itself provide the hardware resource count.

## Cross-cap geometry

[Kobayashi and Zhu](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06917) place the honeycomb
Floquet code on a non-orientable cross-cap. One schedule period acts as
logical `HZ` on the single encoded qubit in their convention. Folding turns
the nonlocal identification into a bilayer geometry.

This gate is not a property of the ordinary orientable torus instance. Its
resource contract includes the cross-cap or folded bilayer connectivity,
schedule, and decoder adapted to that geometry.

## Fixed-point and automorphism frameworks

Automorphism codes describe a protected loop in the space of gapped
Hamiltonians or code frames. Fixed-point path-integral circuits generalize the
idea to broader non-chiral Abelian topological phases and can include
non-Clifford ingredients. These frameworks explain how to design logical
action, but applying them to the original honeycomb memory requires an
explicit schedule and fault-tolerance analysis.

## What is not claimed

The fetch-verified sweep found no complete universal, fully benchmarked
logical gate set for the unmodified planar Hastings-Haah honeycomb memory.
Three nearby results must remain separate:

- Floquet color-code fold and twist gates use a different dynamical family;
- Floquet-Bacon-Shor experiments demonstrate dynamical logical control on a
  different code;
- general non-Clifford fixed-point circuits require added phase resources and
  are not operations of the bare three-round schedule.

The card therefore records only the native anyon exchange, twist-defect
processing, and cross-cap `HZ`, each with its own mechanism and geometry.

## How to verify a proposed operation

A complete operation certificate needs:

1. input and output ISGs;
2. a logical Pauli basis in both frames;
3. redressing rules through every measurement round;
4. the induced symplectic map on logical Paulis;
5. detector definitions during the deformation;
6. a fault-distance or malignant-fault analysis;
7. geometry, time, ancilla, and routing costs.

The current constructor certifies only the undeformed periodic memory.

documents.title: What hardware has and has not demonstrated
documents.markdown:
# What hardware has and has not demonstrated

The word “realized” covers several distinct milestones. This ledger attaches
each source to the strongest claim its protocol supports.

## Literal honeycomb experiment

[Measurements of Floquet Code Plaquette Stabilizers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.13154)
implemented measurements associated with the original honeycomb Floquet code
on IBM Falcon hardware and used changes in inferred plaquette stabilizers as
a noise diagnostic.

Established:

- hardware execution of the relevant parity-measurement pattern;
- reconstruction of plaquette information from outcomes;
- empirical syndrome-change behavior on the tested device.

Not established:

- a full encoded logical honeycomb memory;
- repeated logical error suppression;
- improvement with increasing distance;
- a below-threshold regime;
- logical gates.

The manuscript describes itself as a preliminary study not intended for
journal submission. `card.yaml` records the hardware execution as
`demonstrated` while stating the restricted claim boundary.

## Majorana parity-measurement architectures

Majorana tetrons motivate the code because fermion-parity measurements can be
native. [Karzig et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.05289) develop scalable
protected parity-measurement hardware, while
[Paetznick et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.11829) build planar Floquet
circuits, Majorana fault models, detectors, and overhead comparisons.

These works establish detailed architecture and simulation evidence. They do
not report a laboratory logical honeycomb memory. Poisoning, parity
correlations, and device constraints are part of their conclusions and cannot
be replaced by generic depolarizing noise.

## Spin-optical photonic proposal

[Dessertaine et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.07065) co-design a photonic
architecture and numerically report a `6.4%` photon-loss threshold for their
Floquet implementation. This number is a simulated architecture threshold
under a tailored loss model. It is not a laboratory threshold and does not
transfer to Majorana or superconducting circuits.

## Fabrication-defect and dynamic-circuit proposals

[McLauchlan, Gehér, and Moylett](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15854) provide a
schedule-preserving prescription for removing faulty hardware locations and
simulate tolerance to fabrication defects.
[Claes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.08069) proposes an ancilla-free dynamic
circuit with changing data/measurement roles, leakage removal, and improved
timelike distance.

Both are executable design advances. Neither is a hardware demonstration.
Each changes the detector model compared with the ideal torus constructor.

## Adjacent Floquet experiment

The
[Floquet-Bacon-Shor dynamical-qubit experiment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.03867)
demonstrates universal logical operations with periodic measurements on
superconducting hardware. It is evidence that Floquet control primitives can
work experimentally, but it is a different code with different geometry,
schedule, logical count, and detectors. It is intentionally absent from the
Honeycomb `realizations` facet.

## Status as of the literature sweep

As of the fetch-verified 2026-07-26 sweep, no qualifying experiment
demonstrated a full logical honeycomb memory with repeated error suppression,
distance scaling, or logical gates. This negative result is part of the
entry's knowledge boundary, not a missing citation.

documents.title: Representation dictionary
documents.markdown:
# Representation dictionary

No single representation makes every Honeycomb claim transparent. The useful
maps form a chain, and every arrow has a different proof status.

## Schedule and ISG

**Objects:** measured Pauli words grouped into ordered rounds; a commuting
binary symplectic row space updated after each outcome.

**Best for:** exact round content, commutation within a round, startup rank,
periodic rank, `dynamic_k`, and machine export.

**Atlas status:** executable. `constructor.py`, `Schedule`, and `ISGTracker`
recompute these facts.

**Blind spot:** physical outcome signs, preparation/readout circuits,
detectors, and geometry coordinates are not present.

## Plaquette backbone and moving matching

**Objects:** rank-eight span of weight-six plaquette products plus the
currently measured perfect matching.

**Best for:** understanding the steady ISG rank and why incompatible
measurements do not erase the code.

**Atlas status:** recomputed by `reproduce.py`; the first plaquette words and
all row-space memberships are asserted.

**Blind spot:** the logical anyon labels require the toric-frame conversion.

## Instantaneous toric code

**Map:** contract the just-measured matching and apply local Clifford changes
of basis.

**Best for:** two torus logical qubits, winding strings, topological order, and
the meaning of electric/magnetic labels.

**Atlas status:** curated from Hastings-Haah. The current engine checks the
rank consequence but does not replay the local Clifford circuit.

**Blind spot:** one frame omits measurement faults and logical transport
through time.

## Majorana / parton gauge theory

Represent a spin by four Majoranas `b^x,b^y,b^z,c` with a local parity
constraint. A directional edge term factors schematically as

`sigma_u^a sigma_v^a = (i b_u^a b_v^a)(i c_u c_v)`.

The first factor is a `Z2` gauge link and the second pairs matter Majoranas.
Plaquette products become gauge fluxes. Cycling measurements changes the
pairing pattern.

**Best for:** the local anticommuting edge algebra, gauge-invariant
plaquettes, and weak/coherent-measurement extensions.

**Atlas status:** curated from
[Kitaev](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0506438) and
[later monitored-fermion work](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.08450). There is no
generic fermionic compiler in the repository, so this view is not
machine-derived.

**Blind spot:** a static Kitaev Hamiltonian and a projective measurement
schedule have different dynamics.

## Spacetime detector model

**Map:** compile the physical parity circuit into measurement outcomes,
detector parities, logical observables, and fault-to-detector incidence.

**Best for:** matching, correlations, timelike boundaries, leakage, logical
error rates, and fault distance.

**Atlas status:** literature-curated. The ideal schedule is exported, but no
Honeycomb circuit/DEM is produced by this constructor.

**Blind spot:** detector graphs depend on the circuit and noise model; there
is no circuit-independent threshold graph.

## Anyon automorphism

**Map:** compose the local equivalences between consecutive instantaneous
topological frames.

**Best for:** the `e <-> m` exchange, logical-frame transport, twist defects,
and cross-cap gates.

**Atlas status:** curated from Hastings-Haah and the automorphism-code
framework.

**Blind spot:** naming an automorphism does not supply detector circuits or
hardware costs.

## Measurement QCA

**Objects:** a locality-preserving transformation of quantum information
induced by periodic measurement and classical outcomes.

**Best for:** anomalous boundary information flow and why bulk stabilizer rank
misses boundary dynamics.

**Atlas status:** curated from
[Aasen, Haah, Li, and Mong](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.01277).

**Blind spot:** the classification is coarser than a device noise model.

## ZX spacetime

**Objects:** a graphical tensor network in which parity measurements,
preparations, fusions, and feed-forward are ZX nodes and connections.

**Best for:** relating circuit, measurement-based, fusion-based, and Floquet
protocols by local diagram rewrites.

**Atlas status:** curated from
[Bombin et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.08829); no Honeycomb ZX artifact
ships with the entry.

**Blind spot:** a local diagram equivalence preserves logical structure under
its assumptions, not the numerical noise performance of every physical
realization.

## Conversion ledger

| from | to | status in this entry |
|---|---|---|
| constructor schedule | ideal round/edge export | verified |
| schedule history | steady ISG snapshot | verified |
| face walks | plaquette row space | verified in reproduction |
| steady ISG | toric stabilizers | curated local-Clifford map |
| physical circuit | detector graph | cited, not exported |
| spin Paulis | Majorana gauge variables | curated dictionary |
| period of frames | anyon automorphism | curated |
| measurement protocol | ZX / measurement-QCA | curated |

This ledger prevents a derived rank from lending machine certainty to a
curated conversion farther down the chain.

documents.title: From plaquette coloring to a periodic ISG
documents.markdown:
# From plaquette coloring to a periodic ISG

This page derives the exact finite object built by `constructor.py`. It does
not use the instantaneous toric-code equivalence as a substitute for the
schedule algebra.

## Two labels on every edge

Index the two vertices of cell `(i,j)` by

`A(i,j) = 2(i L2 + j)` and `B(i,j) = A(i,j) + 1`,

with both coordinates reduced periodically. The constructor uses

- `z`: `A(i,j)--B(i,j)`,
- `x`: `B(i,j)--A(i+1,j)`,
- `y`: `B(i,j)--A(i,j+1)`.

Direction fixes the measured operator: `ZZ`, `XX`, or `YY`. This is the first
edge label.

The hexagons are properly colored by `0,1,2`. If an edge separates faces with
colors `a` and `b`, its round label is the missing color

`r = 3 - a - b`.

This is the second edge label. It is transverse to direction: on the shipped
`3 x 3` torus, each round contains three `XX`, three `YY`, and three `ZZ`
measurements.

## Why every round is a perfect matching

At a honeycomb vertex, the three incident edges separate the three pairs of
neighboring face colors: `{0,1}`, `{1,2}`, and `{2,0}`. Their missing colors
are respectively `2`, `0`, and `1`. Exactly one incident edge therefore
belongs to each round.

Consequently, edges with one round label are disjoint and cover every vertex.
Their two-qubit Pauli measurements commute because they have disjoint support.
For `n = 2 L1 L2`, every round contains `n/2 = L1 L2` measurements. The
constructor turns this proof obligation into a hard check by sorting all
round supports and requiring the list `0,...,n-1` exactly once.

## The rank-eight plaquette backbone

For a face `p`, multiply the directional Pauli operator on each of its six
boundary edges. Two different letters meet at every vertex. Their product,
up to a phase omitted by the Atlas sign-free representation, is the third
Pauli letter. The resulting `W_p` has weight six.

There are two commutation cases:

1. A measured boundary edge overlaps `W_p` at two endpoints. Its Pauli letter
   differs from the plaquette letter at each endpoint, so two
   anticommutations cancel.
2. A measured edge leaving the face overlaps at one vertex. Its direction is
   the direction unused by the two boundary edges, exactly the Pauli letter
   left on `W_p` at that vertex, so the local operators commute.

Thus `W_p` commutes with every edge measurement in all rounds.

For the `3 x 3` convention, the first three plaquette words are

```text
XY___ZZ___YX______
_ZXY__YXZ_________
___ZXY__YXZ_______
```

The reproduction script constructs all nine words from the six-edge face
walks. Every word has weight six, all lie in the steady snapshot row space,
and their binary rank is eight. The one dependency is the closed-torus
global product relation.

## The measurement update

Let the current commuting ISG generators be rows `g_i` and let `p` be the next
measured Pauli.

- If `p` commutes with every `g_i` and is outside their span, append it.
- If `p` is already in the span, only its outcome sign changes; the sign-free
  row space stays fixed.
- If `p` anticommutes with generators indexed by a set `A`, choose one pivot
  `g_a`. Replace every other `g_b`, `b in A`, by `g_b g_a`, which now commutes
  with `p`, and replace `g_a` by `p`.

The third rule trades one generator for one measurement rather than
increasing rank. Binary symplectic addition implements multiplication and the
symplectic inner product selects `A`. This is the exact
`ISGTracker.measure` algorithm used by the constructor.

Starting from no generators on the `3 x 3` instance, the ranks after each
complete round are

```text
9, 12, 14, 16, 16, 16,
16, 16, 16, ...
```

Once the rank reaches sixteen, the phase-specific row spaces repeat after
each three-round period. Nine current-round measurements plus eight
plaquette generators have combined rank sixteen, so their spans share one
relation. On eighteen qubits, `dynamic_k = 18 - 16 = 2`.

## The torus coloring constraint

The face-adjacency graph is triangular. In the constructor coordinates, a
valid closed formula is

`c(i,j) = i - j mod 3`.

Transport around the first periodic handle shifts `i` by `L1`; transport
around the second shifts `j` by `L2`. The color returns to itself only if both
lengths vanish modulo three. The constructor also tries the opposite
orientation and constraint propagation, then rejects a torus when no proper
coloring is found.

The reproduction script checks all `2 <= L1,L2 <= 9` face graphs and finds a
coloring exactly when both dimensions are divisible by three. This finite
scan is a regression certificate for the shipped constructor. The winding
argument supplies the reason for its accepted family.

## The direction-grouped counterexample

The most dangerous wrong constructor measures all `XX` direction edges,
then all `YY`, then all `ZZ`. Every round is still a perfect matching.
Plaquette products still commute with every measurement. Those two local
checks therefore cannot distinguish the protocol.

The long-time ISG does. On the `6 x 6` torus:

| grouping | physical qubits | steady ISG rank | `dynamic_k` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| plaquette missing color | 72 | 70 | 2 |
| edge direction / Pauli letter | 72 | 52 | 20 |

Every entry in this table is recomputed by `reproduce.py`. The wrong sequence
is not a small convention change; it preserves an extensive collection of
logical degrees of freedom instead of the two toric logicals.

## What this page establishes

The schedule's correctness is certified by a chain of independent invariants:
proper face coloring, perfect matchings, mixed Pauli content, commuting
plaquette products, startup rank profile, periodic rank, and a counterexample
that passes the local checks but fails the dynamical count. The literature is
needed to interpret the steady ISG as topological order; the finite algebra
above is executable and recomputed.

documents.title: Detectors and distance live in spacetime
documents.markdown:
# Detectors and distance live in spacetime

An instantaneous stabilizer matrix describes which Pauli operators are known
at one time. A noisy Floquet memory is a history of parity measurements.
Distance must therefore distinguish harmless changes of that history from
undetectable histories that act logically.

## From random outcomes to a detector

An edge measurement outcome is not itself a syndrome bit. Even without
physical noise, measuring an operator outside the current ISG can produce a
fresh random sign. The useful invariant is a plaquette product assembled from
edge outcomes in the rounds where its factors were measured.

Let `s_p(t)` be the inferred sign of plaquette `p` after the required outcomes
have become available. A detector compares compatible inferences, for
example

`D_p(t) = s_p(t) s_p(t-Delta)`.

In an ideal history, `D_p(t)=+1`. A fault can flip a collection of nearby
detectors. The exact delay `Delta`, which outcomes enter `s_p`, and the
startup/readout rules belong to the measurement circuit. They are not stored
in the static `CheckMatrix`.

[A Fault-Tolerant Honeycomb Memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.10457)
constructs the periodic detector graphs and correlation-aware matching
problem for explicit circuits. The Atlas schedule export stops one layer
earlier: it gives the ideal measured Paulis and their order.

## Why snapshot distance answers the wrong question

Suppose a Pauli error has low weight on one time slice. Three cases are
possible:

1. it creates detectors and is therefore visible;
2. it can be absorbed into changes of measurement outcomes or stabilizer
   representatives without changing encoded information;
3. it creates no detector but transports or flips a logical class.

Only the third case is a logical fault. A minimum-weight normalizer element
of one snapshot does not account for faulty measurements, errors extended
over several rounds, or equivalences that move faults through the measurement
history.

Blackwell and Haah formalize this distinction in
[The Code Distance of Floquet Codes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05549).
Their distance minimizes the weight of an undetectable **non-benign**
spacetime error. Benign errors form the equivalence class that neither
changes detector data nor acts on the encoded information.

## Three quantities that must not be collapsed

| quantity | formal input | question answered |
|---|---|---|
| snapshot `k` | one steady ISG | how many logical qubits exist in this frame? |
| `dynamic_k` | repeated ideal schedule | how many logical qubits survive continued measurement? |
| circuit fault distance | full noisy spacetime protocol | what is the lightest undetectable non-benign fault history? |

The current Atlas engine recomputes the first two. It has no generic
spacetime benign-error quotient, so the third remains an honest gap. Recording
a static exact distance under property `d` would attach machine certainty to
the wrong object.

## What a replayable fault-distance artifact needs

A future verifier must receive at least:

1. preparation and final-readout conventions;
2. the physical measurement circuit for every ideal parity operator;
3. a named fault alphabet and location weights;
4. detector definitions, including temporal boundaries;
5. logical observables in the chosen input/output frames;
6. benign generators or an equivalent quotient rule;
7. an exact or bounded search with a replayable witness.

The result should be keyed by circuit and observation window, not placed as a
family-wide scalar on the honeycomb check matrix. This missing engine is
tracked by the project's Floquet fault-distance Wanted item.

## Decoder consequence

The instantaneous toric map is still useful: it predicts topological detector
structure and helps identify logical homology classes. It does not remove the
time coordinate. A matching graph for the honeycomb memory includes
spacelike and timelike edges, correlations from two-qubit measurements, and
special nodes at boundaries. Rebuilding that graph after a circuit change is
part of the code definition at the fault-tolerant level.

documents.title: The instantaneous toric frame and its anyon automorphism
documents.markdown:
# The instantaneous toric frame and its anyon automorphism

The steady ISG is locally equivalent to a toric code after every round, but
the equivalence itself moves. Keeping those two facts together explains both
memory and logical-frame motion.

## Contract the latest matching

Immediately after round `r`, every measured edge in matching `M_r` has a
known two-qubit parity. Regard its two endpoints as one effective qubit.
Because `M_r` is a perfect matching, this contraction covers the lattice
without overlap.

The measured parity fixes one Pauli degree of freedom inside each pair. A
depth-one product of two-qubit Clifford changes of basis can send that parity
to a single-qubit stabilizer on an auxiliary degree of freedom, leaving the
other degree of freedom as the effective qubit. This is a local change of
basis, not a projection that discards logical information.

Under this map:

- products of neighboring honeycomb plaquettes become one family of toric
  stabilizers;
- compatible products involving the current matching become the conjugate
  family;
- noncontractible dressed strings become toric winding strings.

The resulting torus has two anticommuting winding pairs and therefore two
logical qubits. Hastings and Haah give the explicit local-Clifford
identification in
[Dynamically Generated Logical Qubits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.02194).
The Atlas constructor currently verifies the ISG rank, not the Clifford
circuit, so `card.yaml` marks this view as curated.

## Logical representatives must be redressed

A fixed physical Pauli string need not commute with the next round. If a
representative crosses an incoming measured edge with the wrong local Pauli,
multiply it by current ISG generators until it commutes with the entire
incoming matching. Multiplication changes the physical string but not its
logical class in the current code.

This redressing is the logical-operator analogue of the generator update in
the ISG tracker. It is why the statement “the same logical string survives”
is misleading. What survives is an equivalence class transported through a
sequence of changing stabilizer quotients.

## One period exchanges electric and magnetic labels

The effective toric lattice after round `r+1` is not identified with the
effective lattice after round `r` by the identity map. Composing the three
local changes of frame around one period exchanges the electric and magnetic
anyon types:

`e -> m`, `m -> e`, and `em -> em`.

On logical Paulis, the same action exchanges the two conjugate winding
characters, up to the chosen cycle basis and outcome-dependent Pauli frame.
The anyon label therefore closes after two periods, not one.

This is a protected automorphism of the topological order, as organized by
[Aasen, Wang, and Hastings](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11137). It is a logical
operation performed by continued memory cycling, but it is not a claim that
every physical logical representative literally returns after six rounds.

## What the equivalence does not imply

The instantaneous toric frame establishes:

- topological order at a fixed steady time;
- two torus logical qubits;
- string-like logical representatives and their anyon labels;
- a local route for comparing consecutive frames.

It does not establish:

- the detector graph of a noisy parity-measurement circuit;
- circuit fault distance or threshold;
- the behavior of a planar boundary;
- a complete universal logical gate set;
- equivalence to the static Kitaev honeycomb Hamiltonian dynamics.

Those require spacetime, boundary, or circuit data. The distinction is why
`instances.yaml` verifies `k` and `dynamic_k` but leaves `d` unclaimed.

## A useful transport test

To analyze a proposed schedule modification:

1. identify the effective code after each round;
2. choose a basis of logical winding classes;
3. redress each representative to commute with the next measurements;
4. express the transported classes in the next basis;
5. compose the induced symplectic maps over the full period.

Preserving the ISG rank checks only that information survives. The composed
map determines what logical automorphism was performed.
